hypotheses.justification: `[CartesianMonoidalCategory K]` already provides this instance. Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Basic.lean (line 505) has `instance (priority := 100) : Limits.HasFiniteProducts C` for any `CartesianMonoidalCategory C`. It is built from `tensorProductIsBinaryProduct` and the terminal unit. `HasBinaryProducts K` is the reducible abbreviation `HasLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) K`, which instance search gets from `hasLimitsOfShape_discrete` in Limits/Shapes/FiniteProducts.lean (`[HasFiniteProducts C] (ι) [Finite ι] : HasLimitsOfShape (Discrete ι) C`). So without the binder, `tensorLeftIsoProd A` (which requires `[HasBinaryProducts C]`) and `prod.fst` still elaborate. These classes are all `Prop`s, so by proof irrelevance the resulting statement is definitionally the same as the original. The proof is unchanged. `conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom_comp` with `limit.isLimit _` and `⟨.left⟩` works for whatever `HasLimit (pair A B)` instance is found, and the definition of `tensorLeftIsoProd` unfolds to `conePointUniqueUpToIso` against that same `limit.isLimit`. No degenerate cases arise: the statement is a morphism equation with no side conditions.
